title: Closure of a Savings or Money Market Account and Payout of the Balance
content:
### The owner's decision

Closing an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is the owner's own decision. The agent registers a closure request in pending customer confirmation status, naming the disbursement method, and the account closes only after the owner confirms it.

### Before the account closes

An account that is the overdraft protection source of a checking account is unlinked on that checking account before it closes.

### The early closure fee

The early closure fee applies when the account is closed within the tier's early closure window in calendar days after the account was opened. Calendar days are counted with the day after the opening date as day 1, and the fee applies when the closure date is on or before the opening date plus the tier's early closure window. The comparison is not-later-than, so a closure on the last day of the window carries the fee.

The fee is written with the early closure fee code before the payout, and is reduced so that it never takes the balance below zero.

### The payout

Accrued interest since the last cycle close is credited first, and only on a tier whose accrued interest parameter reads yes. The remaining balance is then paid out in full as one withdrawal, either by internal transfer to a Piedmont Crescent Bank account of the same customer or by official check mailed to the address on file. The account closes at zero, with its automatic transfer stopped.

A payout never counts toward the withdrawal allowance and never incurs an excess withdrawal fee.

### Boundary of the early closure window

Take a hypothetical account opened on 1 May whose tier carries an early closure window of 90 calendar days. Day 1 of the window is 2 May, and the opening date plus 90 calendar days falls on 30 July. A closure dated 30 July carries the early closure fee; a closure dated 31 July does not.
